headline: Range grows volumes and prices but income slips on hedges
summary_short: Range Resources reported Q2 2026 revenue from natural gas, NGLs and oil sales of $702.1M (+5.3% y/y) on 4.5% higher production and 2.0% higher net realized prices, but net income fell 17.8% y/y to $195.3M ($0.83 diluted EPS) as derivative fair value income dropped to $73.5M from $154.7M a year earlier.
summary_long: Revenue growth was driven by 5% higher production (new wells outpacing decline) plus 2% higher net realized prices (including derivative settlements and transport). Net income fell to $195.3M from $237.6M, attributed to lower derivative fair value income ($73.5M vs $154.7M). Total costs and expenses rose 5.5% on higher direct operating expense (water hauling, labor, workovers) and G&A (employee costs, legal). Operating cash flow was $235.0M, down $101.2M y/y on timing and working-capital changes. Range repurchased $78.4M of stock (2.0M shares) and paid a $0.10/share dividend, up 11% y/y. No forward guidance was given beyond reaffirming the 2026 capital program is funded from operating cash flow.
